transcript.text:
Thank you all for your findings. Let me summarize what's on the record so far before I make my decision.

Jonah, you've stated that the borrower's owners will fund exactly $750,000 of new cash at closing — that's the borrower cash injection.

Nadia, you've stated that loan operations can enforce a weekly borrowing-base certificate, the risk team requires it weekly, and the operating instruction for it is missing from the draft closing checklist and must be added before close.

Ravi, you've stated that your revised downside analysis supports approval only with a 6-month extension, an exactly $1,000,000 principal paydown, and an 850-basis-point cash interest rate.

I need to flag a few things before settling. The borrower requested a 12-month extension and a reduced cash interest rate, but Ravi's credit risk finding only supports a 6-month extension and an 850 bps cash rate — which is an increase, not a reduction. Also, the current loan documents don't specify a principal paydown or borrower cash contribution, so the $1,000,000 paydown and $750,000 cash injection are new terms we'd need to document.

Before I can close the restructuring, the approval checklist requires each consulted function's finding to be stated in the meeting record, and I must cite each one in my final justification. I believe we now have findings from credit risk (Ravi), loan operations (Nadia), and relationship management (Jonah). However, I do not yet have a stated finding from banking counsel. Per our normal process, I need counsel's input before I can settle this package.

Additionally, Nadia's point about the missing weekly borrowing-base certificate instruction on the closing checklist needs to be resolved.

Can banking counsel provide their finding? And once that's on the record, I'll be in a position to make the binding underwriting decision.

transcript.text: I need to put my banking counsel finding on the record. This week I discovered that an existing equipment lender's intercreditor agreement requires three distinct closing-package items before we can proceed: first, the equipment lender's written consent before any maturity extension is granted; second, an amended-loan prohibition on additional liens on the borrower's production equipment; and third, a separate intercreditor-consent commitment recorded in the closing package. My legal note has not yet been circulated, but this is my formal finding — all three items must be satisfied and documented in the closing package before this restructuring can close. This is particularly relevant given that the borrower has requested a maturity extension, which triggers the equipment lender's consent requirement.
